rounds.text: Shoppers Stop Ltd demonstrates exceptional cash-generation capability, posting an operating cash flow of Rs 838 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs 703 Cr in Mar 2026 [E32, E33], with operating cash flow reaching 112% of operating profit [E34]. Momentum is backed by quantitative screening where the rules-based screen scores 76 out of 100 with a medium confidence BUY rating [E57], driven by year-over-year sales growth of 11% and net profit growth of 12% [E58, E59], alongside quarter-over-quarter improvements in both metrics [E60, E61]. Institutional confidence is actively building, demonstrated by domestic institutions increasing their stake to 25.70% from 21.57% [E41], promoter holdings rising to 66.06% [E39], and overall institutional money flow registering as positive [E42]. On a structural level, the company benefits from a broader Consumer Services sector tailwind with a tailwind score of +0.54 [E66], while its valuation holds an attractive EV/EBITDA of 9.57x compared to the sector benchmark of 12.02x [E10]. Conceded: debt-to-equity is elevated at 11.40x with borrowings at Rs 3,317 Cr [E35, E37], current liabilities exceed current assets with a current ratio of 0.85x [E36], and the price-to-book ratio is an elevated 14.58x against a sector benchmark of 2.27x [E1, E6].

Shoppers Stop Ltd carries severe balance sheet risks and a lofty valuation that are entirely unsupported by its fundamental performance. The company exhibits a staggering debt-to-equity ratio of 11.40x with borrowings sitting at Rs 3,317 Cr [E35, E37], while its current ratio of 0.85x reveals that current liabilities exceed current assets [E36]. Profitability metrics are deeply concerning, highlighted by a negative return on equity of -6.11% and an ROA of -0.55%, both lagging significantly behind sector benchmarks [E7, E8]. Furthermore, the twelve-month compounded profit growth cratered by -205% [E18], and the stock suffers from a low interest coverage ratio [E55]. Despite this weak earnings profile and a long-term 10-year sales growth rate of just 1% [E13], the stock trades at an exorbitant price-to-book ratio of 14.6x against a sector benchmark of 2.27x [E6], accompanied by a twelve-month price return of -26.0% [E47] and a painful historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -88.8% [E48]. The bear overlooks the extraordinary cash generation powering this operation, evidenced by operating cash flow of Rs 838 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 703 Cr in Mar 2026 [E32, E33], with operating cash flow reaching 112% of operating profit [E34]. Long-term top-line metrics display strong momentum, achieving a 24% compounded sales growth rate over 5 years [E14] alongside a current 10% growth rate in the trailing twelve months [E16]. Institutional confidence remains robust, demonstrated by domestic institutions increasing their stake to 25.70% from 21.57% [E41], positive institutional money flow [E42], and high promoter ownership at 66.06% [E39]. Furthermore, the sector operates in a favorable macro TAILWIND [E66], and the quantitative rules-based screen explicitly rates the stock a BUY with a score of 76 out of 100 [E57].

Conceded: [E32], [E33], [E34], [E41], [E42], [E66]. The bull points to robust cash generation and institutional accumulation, but glosses over the severe structural leverage risks and poor capital efficiency haunting the balance sheet, such as a debt-to-equity ratio of 11.40x where total borrowings sit at ₹ 3,317 Cr [E35, E37]. While 5-year sales growth looks strong at 24% [E14], the longer 10-year compounded sales growth crawls at a meager 1% [E13], and trailing twelve-month profit growth collapsed by -205% [E18]. This deteriorating profitability contributes to a negative ROE of -6.11% [E8] and a low ROCE of 7.08% [E9], both falling well behind sector benchmarks [E8, E9]. Furthermore, foreign institutional investors have fled, slashing their holdings from 6.78% to 1.92% [E40], while the stock demands a bloated price-to-book multiple of 14.6x against a sector median of just 2.27x [E6].
